judgments.yea_description: Voted to pass Senate Bill 8. It requires owners to lock a gun when a minor, at-risk person, or person banned from having guns may reach it, with exceptions for carrying, self-defense, or illegal entry. Penalties are up to $500, $1,000 if someone gets the gun, and $10,000 if it causes harm or a crime; lost or stolen guns must be reported within 48 hours instead of 72. The Illinois Senate passed it 33-19, and it became law.

judgments.yea_description: Voted to pass House Bill 1373. Police must trace a gun that was illegally held or used, found at a crime scene, linked to a crime, or found abandoned, lost, or thrown away to learn its source and past owners. They must use the federal Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives eTrace system and share trace reports with other Illinois police agencies that also share their data. The Illinois House passed it 75-40, and it became law.

judgments.yea_description: Voted to pass the House version of House Bill 5295. It made health networks separate abortion-related records and block sharing outside Illinois, unless the patient chose a specific out-of-state provider. The House passed it 73-34; the Senate later changed key definitions and access rules, and that final version became law effective July 1, 2027.
judgments.nay_description: Voted against the House version of House Bill 5295. It made health networks separate abortion-related records and block sharing outside Illinois, unless the patient chose a specific out-of-state provider. The House passed it 73-34; the Senate later changed key definitions and access rules, and that final version became law effective July 1, 2027.

judgments.yea_description: Voted to pass the Senate version of House Bill 5295. It requires electronic health networks to segregate coded abortion and gender-dysphoria health records and block out-of-state sharing, except for technical support, quality assurance, payment operations, or with patient consent, and lets patients sue. The Senate passed it 38-19; the House agreed, and it became law effective July 1, 2027.

judgments.yea_description: Voted to pass Senate Bill 3341. It lets any minor consent to birth control without anyone else's approval and gives the minor adult legal authority for that care. Prescription birth control must be requested from a licensed doctor, advanced-practice nurse, physician assistant, or pharmacist acting under pharmacy law. The Illinois Senate passed it 37-19, and it became law.

judgments.yea_description: Voted to pass the Senate version of Senate Bill 3777. It made rules that cause a discriminatory effect a civil-rights violation in jobs, credit, and public places, even without discriminatory intent. The Senate passed it 38-20; the House later added a narrower proof test and named citizenship, family duties, work permission, arrest records, and conviction records, and that version became law.
judgments.nay_description: Voted against the Senate version of Senate Bill 3777. It made rules that cause a discriminatory effect a civil-rights violation in jobs, credit, and public places, even without discriminatory intent. The Senate passed it 38-20; the House later added a narrower proof test and named citizenship, family duties, work permission, arrest records, and conviction records, and that version became law.

judgments.yea_description: Voted to pass the House version of Senate Bill 3777. It bars job, credit, and public-place rules that unfairly harm protected groups, including citizenship, family duties, work permission, arrest records, and conviction records. A business may defend a needed job rule, but a complainant can show a less discriminatory option; the House passed it 72-38, the Senate agreed, and it became law.
judgments.nay_description: Voted against the House version of Senate Bill 3777. A business may defend a needed job rule, but a complainant can show a less discriminatory option; the House passed it 72-38, the Senate agreed, and it became law.

judgments.yea_description: Voted to pass Senate Bill 1976. It stops state agencies from weakening worker-pay or coal-mine safety rules below federal protections in place on April 28, 2025, unless a later state law allows it. It also orders Illinois to replace revoked federal workplace-safety rules, allows lawsuits and penalties, and lets the labor director copy a federal rule as it stood before repeal or change. The Illinois Senate passed it 38-19, and it became law.

The Illinois Senate passed it 38-19, and it became law.

judgments.yea_description: Voted to pass the Senate version of Senate Bill 2339. It limited extra E-Verify checks, protected workers responding to federal ID mismatches, and added Labor Department enforcement, civil fines, private lawsuits, and a minor criminal penalty. The Senate passed it 35-21; the House later removed the E-Verify limits and criminal penalty, and that narrower version became law.

judgments.yea_description: Voted to pass Senate Bill 3772. For air permits requested on or after January 1, 2027, the state must study effects on communities flagged for unfair pollution burdens, the applicant's past record, and whether more tests or changes are needed. It also creates an Environmental Justice Office and officer to coordinate this work across state environmental programs. The Illinois Senate passed it 43-11, and it became law.
judgments.nay_description: Voted against Senate Bill 3772. For air permits requested on or after January 1, 2027, the state must study effects on communities flagged for unfair pollution burdens, the applicant's past record, and whether more tests or changes are needed. It also creates an Environmental Justice Office and officer to coordinate this work across state environmental programs. The Illinois Senate passed it 43-11, and it became law.

judgments.yea_description: Voted to pass Senate Bill 3772. For air-pollution construction permits sought on or after January 1, 2027 by sources in areas flagged for unfair pollution burdens, the state must notify the community, weigh whether emissions can be cut, and decide whether more air modeling is needed. It must also weigh the applicant's past record of environmental violations before issuing a permit. It creates an Environmental Justice Office and officer inside the state environmental agency. The Illinois House passed it 73-39, and it became law.
judgments.nay_description: Voted against Senate Bill 3772. The Illinois House passed it 73-39, and it became law.
